record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.context_brief: MSSM baryon/lepton violation and matter parity
record.original_question: In the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, the most general renormalizable superpotential allows baryon-number-violating and lepton-number-violating interactions that together would mediate very rapid proton decay through squark-suppressed operators. What exact symmetry or mechanism forbids the dangerous simultaneous baryon and lepton violation, can that symmetry be understood as a gauge-protected discrete symmetry rather than an ad hoc global rule, and how should higher-dimension proton-decay operators and lightest-superpartner stability be controlled at the same time?

evidence.quote: Question #1 Why doesn’t the proton decay in 10−17 years?

Allowing simultaneous B- and L-violation would be a disaster. For example, given non-zero λ and λ′′, one can form a four-fermion operator QudL which can mediate proton decay and is only suppressed by squark masses, not MGUT or MPl.

Fortunately it is easy to invent a new discrete symmetry which simultaneously forbids all the unwanted terms and which allows those that are phenomenologically necessary. This is ‘matter parity,’ a Z2 symmetry under which all the matter fields (L, e, Q, u, d) are odd and the Higgs fields are even.

Thus far, we have said nothing about proton decay from higher-dimension operators. In particular there are many terms of dimension five which are invariant under matter parity which can mediate proton decay.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) with chiral matter superfields Q, u^c, d^c, L, e^c (in the usual Standard-Model gauge representations) and Higgs doublet superfields H_u, H_d. The most general renormalizable gauge-invariant superpotential admits the baryon-number-violating couplings λ''_{ijk} u^c_i d^c_j d^c_k and the lepton-number-violating couplings λ_{ijk} L_i L_j e^c_k, λ'_{ijk} L_i Q_j d^c_k, and μ_i L_i H_u. Simultaneously turning on a baryon-violating coupling λ'' and a lepton-violating coupling λ' generates an effective four-fermion operator (QudL-type) that mediates proton decay suppressed only by squark masses, producing a proton lifetime grossly inconsistent with experiment.

(a) Determine a discrete symmetry imposed on the MSSM superfields that simultaneously forbids all of the dangerous renormalizable B- and L-violating couplings while permitting all phenomenologically required Yukawa interactions and the μ-term.

(b) Determine whether such a discrete symmetry can be realized as the unbroken subgroup of a spontaneously broken continuous gauge symmetry (i.e. a discrete gauge symmetry, free of mixed gauge–discrete anomalies), so that it is protected against violation by quantum-gravity effects, rather than being imposed as an ad hoc global rule.

(c) Identify a discrete symmetry (or combination of symmetries) that, in addition to forbidding the dangerous dimension-four operators, also forbids or sufficiently suppresses the dimension-five proton-decay operators QQQL and u^c u^c d^c e^c, while still guaranteeing the absolute stability of the lightest superpartner so as to provide a viable dark-matter candidate.
artifact.category_tag: Supersymmetric model building / discrete gauge symmetries
artifact.status_search_result: Discrete-gauge candidates that simultaneously address dimension-four and dimension-five proton-decay operators while preserving LSP stability have been constructed: in particular, proton hexality (P₆) and discrete R-symmetries such as Z₄^R have been identified as anomaly-free discrete gauge symmetries forbidding all dangerous dimension-four operators and the dimension-five proton-decay operators, with matter parity arising as a subgroup. Classifications of anomaly-free Z_N (R-)symmetries of the MSSM have been carried out. However, no single uniquely preferred symmetry has been established experimentally, and the question of the "correct" discrete gauge symmetry of the MSSM remains a topic of ongoing model-building work, so the broader question is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Gauged Discrete Symmetries and Proton Stability
status_evidence.snippet: Anomaly-free Abelian Z_N discrete symmetries leading to automatic R-parity conservation and preventing dangerous higher-dimensional proton-decay operators.
status_evidence.claim: Anomaly-free discrete gauge symmetries forbidding both dim-4 and dim-5 proton decay operators have been constructed.

status_evidence.title: What is the Discrete Gauge Symmetry of the MSSM?
status_evidence.snippet: Proton hexality P_6 proposed as discrete gauge symmetry of the MSSM, forbidding dim-5 proton decay operators in addition to dim-4.
status_evidence.claim: Proton hexality is a preferred anomaly-free Z_6 discrete gauge symmetry that improves on R-parity.

status_evidence.title: R-parity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Matter parity / R-parity is a Z_2 symmetry forbidding renormalizable B- and L-violating couplings; dimension-5 operators remain a concern.
status_evidence.claim: Matter parity solves the dimension-4 problem but does not address dimension-5 operators.
